question: The length of a diagonal of a quadrilateral is 30 m and length of the perpendiculars from two vertices to the diagonal are 15 m and 25 m. Find the area of the quadrilateral.
solution:
**Given:**

Length of a diagonal = 30 m

Length of the perpendiculars from two vertices to the diagonal = 15 m and 25 m

**Formula Used:**

Area of a quadrilateral = 12×Diagonal×(Sum of lengths of perpendiculars)" id="MathJax-Element-11-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">12×Diagonal×(Sum of lengths of perpendiculars)12×Diagonal×(Sum of lengths of perpendiculars)
 \frac{1}{2} \times \text{Diagonal} \times (\text{Sum of lengths of perpendiculars})

**Calculation:**

Diagonal (d) = 30 m

Sum of lengths of perpendiculars = 15 m + 25 m

Sum of lengths of perpendiculars = 40 m

Area of the quadrilateral

⇒ Area = 12×30×40" id="MathJax-Element-12-Frame" role="presentation" style="position: relative;" tabindex="0">12×30×4012×30×40
 \frac{1}{2} \times 30 \times 40

⇒ Area = 15 × 40

⇒ Area = 600 m²

**The area of the quadrilateral is 600 m².**
